cases.difference: Go now accepts literal indexed/mapped/nested property paths with Missing/Null preservation, exposes root/path property names and declared result types, registers explicit field/path/method accessors (including nested explicit schemas), discovers JavaBean GetX/IsX properties into metadata, resolves registered nested fragments through GetFragment, includes accessor/nested metadata in plan canonical identity, and renders schema/map/struct/array/nested values as bounded JSON/XML with title, indent and XML attribute options. The selected Java EventInfra/EventRender/EventJson/EventXML suites and the JavaBean/EXPLICIT/PUBLIC accessor regressions provide the oracle set; complete fragment/metadata integration for XML/Avro/JSON representations, DOM/XPath and exact shared render trace remain open.

Go now recursively converts declared JSON fields into typed slices/arrays/maps/structs, enum-like string aliases, time.Time, big.Int and big.Rat, preserves null pointers, accepts Java-style scalar string coercions, reports invalid scalar/array conversions, maps incompatible object/array shapes to Null, rejects trailing data, supports optional max depth and unknown-field rejection, and renders arbitrary-precision values as JSON numbers. Java's JSON suite has 13 JUnit entries in the selected run and additionally covers provided-underlying class/list adapters, full dynamic JSON value matrix, exact BigDecimal/BigInteger formatting, recursive schema inheritance and event sender integration; shared parse-write trace remains open.

Go now builds an in-memory XML tree with local-name attributes as @name, repeated children as []any, nested indexed paths and a configurable depth bound while keeping the previous scalar leaf-field behavior. The selected Java XML suite ran 33/33 and additionally covers XPath/DOM getters, namespaces, event transpose, XSD-backed schema and fragment semantics; these remain open for shared trace parity.

Go adds WithSchemaParent/NewSchemaWithOptions, parent-first field flattening, inherited dynamic policy, ParentNames metadata, ObjectArray positional inheritance and parent-aware plan canonicalization. Java covers multi-level/branched/cross-module inheritance, configuration-time versus runtime registration, dynamic parent/child properties and nested arrays/objects; those remain open for shared trace parity.

Go now expresses the selected derived-view statistics as analyzable chainable aggregates over Window: CountAll for size, existing sum/count/avg/variance/stddev/weighted average primitives, and new Correlation/Correl plus LinearRegression/Linest with Slope and YIntercept accessors. Length-window eviction recomputes both new and old aggregate rows and the Java ViewDerived regression values are checked with a documented floating-point tolerance. Native Esper derived-view event-type properties, grouped/reclaim/union/intersect/batch iterator behavior and exact NaN/decimal/trace policy remain open.

Go covers the core fluent retention windows and adds UniqueBy/FirstUniqueBy with state-aware multi-key identity, stable key order, Snapshot/Prev history visibility and recursive GroupWindow unique history. GroupWindow keys now use typed/content-preserving identity, including array keys. NamedWindowRetention now supports Unique/FirstUnique replacement state, including content-based array keys, old-stream dispatch and stable snapshots. Named-window-backed and regular event-stream subqueries now support aggregate WindowValues projection as one inner row over the retained group and array-key Unique count filtering, with statement-owned independent source-window state. The Dataflow graph path now gives each Dataflow instance a statement-owned registry with independent state per subquery definition, reproducing the Java array-key Unique window/captive emitter trace. TimeOrder now sorts external timestamps, expires on virtual time, immediately removes late events at the boundary, supports calendar years/months/days with exact AddDate boundaries, and preserves independent grouped-partition lifecycle and iteration order. TimeToLiveAt now models Java #timetolive(timestamp) as an absolute epoch-millisecond expiry, including same-boundary batch removal, already-expired insertion and named-window retention. RankWindowBy now models Java rank unique-key replacement, grouped partition state, sort ordering, full-window pass-through and worst-entry eviction; Sort and Rank preserve their different same-sort-value arrival order and eviction rules. Rank previous access now has Java ViewRankedPrev coverage for PrevWindow and Prev(0..4), while grouped Rank covers per-partition unique-key replacement and eviction. Go now also models the Java TimeOrder previous/prior split: Prev/PrevTail/PrevWindow use the view's sorted head-to-tail access order, Prior uses arrival order, PrevCount follows retained access history, and old-stream expiry rows retain only the Java-available prior value. The new navigation tests cover the two ViewTimeOrderTTLPreviousAndPrior scenes, including Snapshot and expiry lifecycle. Go tests also exercise object-array, two-dimensional-array, rank array unique keys, and stable union/intersection composition over array-key Unique children. Java's selected ViewMultikeyWArray/ViewRank additionally covers context/pattern subquery combinations, wider navigation combinations and exact shared trace; those combinations remain open.

Go extends the Java array-key named-window scenario through fluent MergeIntoNamedWindowWhen: unique-key replacement emits old/new rows, not-matched collisions preserve the replacement old stream, and FirstUnique ignores duplicate inserts. Full Java on-trigger merge/update/delete matrix and shared trace remain open.

The Go fluent chain projects TimeOrder old-stream rows into a registered OrderedStream map and consumes them as new downstream events, covering out-of-order timestamps, equal-timestamp stability, immediate late-event removal and virtual-clock expiry boundaries. Full Java shared trace, representation variants and broader insert-into chains remain open.

The Go fluent Named Window chain models rank retention with unique-key replacement, stable sort/tie eviction, capacity old-stream removal, direct delete routing and iterator snapshots. The Java execution is covered as an exact lifecycle slice; broader rank view context/pattern/subquery combinations and a shared Java/Go trace remain open.

The Go fluent RankWindowBy trace covers descending rank replacement, full-window pass-through, equal-sort arrival order, stable in-place replacement and worst-entry old-stream eviction over the complete Java event sequence. Broader rank navigation/context combinations and shared Java/Go trace serialization remain open.

The Go fluent RankWindowBy trace covers multiple unique-key expressions and multiple ascending sort keys, including a new event immediately evicted as the worst row, replacement old/new pairs and equal-sort tie eviction. The wider Java ViewRank navigation/context/subquery matrix and shared trace remain open.

Context partitions now own independent event-stream subquery registries: inner LastEvent updates broadcast only to active partitions, while a newly created partition starts empty and later outer events reuse its local state. Daily temporal Context termination and next-calendar-window recreation reset the same state, including events received while inactive. Event-driven initiated Context start/end also releases and recreates the registry state. A global Named Window subquery is evaluated from the current global snapshot in every active Context partition, matching the unshared/shared source shape at the value level. The Java ContextInitTermSubqueryInFilter source additionally requires same-context Named Window and not-exists filtering; Named Window index-sharing performance, Context-scoped Named Window retention, pattern Context and the wider Java context/subquery matrix remain open.

The Java filter execution's event-stream Filter, Named Window Filter and Named Window Pattern branches now share one exact tryAssertion trace; NamedWindowRetention(LastEvent()) replaces the previous row and dispatches the old/new state needed by the subquery. Event-stream SubquerySum over a length(2) source reproduces the Java rolling aggregate filter sequence across empty, replacement and exact-sum boundaries, while a chainable Func1 receives a Named Window SubqueryCount inside a Pattern predicate and verifies current Named Window state. Build-time validation now rejects unbounded non-aggregated event-stream subqueries, consumer-local data windows on Named Window subqueries, and incompatible IN/ANY/ALL operand types, matching the mapped EPLSubselectInvalid boundaries. Pattern aggregation, broader Pattern/Context/Dataflow combinations, full parser diagnostics and complete execution-trace/cardinality parity remain open.

C), permuted repeated branches (permute(A,B)* C), nested repeated groups ((A B)* C), and Java finite range expansion (A{2,3} B). The assertions follow Java RowRecogNFAView.step: consume each current state, charge every successor before the next event evaluates it, and release terminal successors. Full Java plan introspection, dynamic quantifiers, branch ordering and all interval/termination compositions remain open.

Go covers a bounded high-partition lifecycle trace with chainable PartitionBy/AllMatches, completed A-B pairs, and a second wave of pending A states followed by partition-local B completion. The Java stress cardinality and runtime-specific partition repository thresholds still require a dedicated performance/reclamation harness.

The pinned Java esperio-csv Maven module passed its 80-test suite. Go covers the CSV/File source, unformatted line source, sink, title/column mapping, quoted rows, typed/custom conversion, loop/reset, fixed-rate and timestamp replay, EOF, engine bridge, Esper Event/Row conversion, and OPENED/STARTED/PAUSED/DESTROYED lifecycle. The remaining connector transports, dataflow graph operator/marker integration, Java bean population and full adapter coordinator parity remain open.

Go covers caller-owned database/sql executors, DML 1-based bindings, nested properties, cancellation, retry, lifecycle, update-then-insert upsert and a real MySQL Docker round trip. The Java esperio-db module ran 4 tests: TestDBAdapterUpsert passed; TestConfig has a platform/JDK-dependent Properties.toString ordering difference and TestDBAdapterDML has a database assertion mismatch in the current environment. Java asynchronous ExecutorServices, XML/config parser, connection-factory settings, SQL type binding, duplicate-row/error handlers and full shared trace remain open.

Go covers a standard-library HTTP client sink with sorted query encoding, stream/property URI templates, JSON request bodies, bounded responses, retry and lifecycle, plus an HTTP server source with method/path/query/header/body capture, pause/stop/restart and an Engine bridge. The pinned Java esperio-http module ran 4 tests: 3 passed and TestHTTPAdapterOutput failed in the current environment due to the legacy subscription/URI compile and connection setup path. Java XML configuration, classic HTTP service handler behavior, async delivery, response/error mapping and full shared trace remain open.

Go covers a concurrent TCP source with key/value CSV, property-ordered CSV, stream-prefixed JSON, Java escape decoding, typed Engine record materialization, multiple clients, pause/resume, stop/restart and a registered object decoder. Java's OBJECT mode uses Java serialization; Go intentionally requires an explicit ObjectDecoder or uses a Go gob fallback, so Java serialization wire compatibility is out of scope. XML configuration/plugin loading, writable-property cache parity, backlog/host binding details, full malformed-input diagnostics and shared Java/Go trace remain open.

Go provides a provider-neutral process-outside bridge contract for Map/Text/Object/Bytes messages, Java InputAdapter event-type property names, DecodeAny/JSON/Object hooks, acknowledge-after-process, retry, pause/resume, factory restart, Engine bridge and deterministic Map/Text output. The Java esperio-springjms module ran 4 tests with 1 pass and 3 failures in the current ActiveMQ/JMX and message-type-marker environment. JVM JMS provider/session/transaction semantics, Spring XML context/plugin loading, listener container recovery and Java Serializable compatibility remain open.

Go covers a RabbitMQ amqp091-go Consumer/Publisher bridge, Java-style host/port/user/vhost and queue/exchange declaration, generated queues, prefetch, JSON/GOB codec hooks, Engine bridge, auto-ack or manual ack-after-process/immediate modes, reject/requeue, retry, pause/resume, factory restart, ordered JSON sink output and real RabbitMQ source/sink round-trips. The Java esperio-amqp module compiles, but the initial Maven run has 5/5 errors without a broker; after RabbitMQ startup the legacy end-to-end suite does not produce a completed count and remains blocked in its receiver wait/QueueingConsumer harness. Java Serializable wire compatibility, Dataflow graph/operator registration, reconnect/connection recovery and shared Java/Go trace remain open.

Go covers a kafka-go-backed Reader/Writer bridge, injected reader/writer contracts, JSON processor, Engine map/struct bridge, commit-after-processing, immediate commit mode, retry, timestamp hook, source factory restart, producer JSON encoding with ordered schema fields, keys/headers and lifecycle. With a single-node Kafka 3.8.1 KRaft broker and four pre-created input topics, the Java esperio-kafka module ran 6/6 and the Go Docker round-trip passed. An initial no-broker/no-topic run is retained as an external environment diagnostic, not a semantic failure. Consumer group/rebalance/offset recovery, custom Java serializer/deserializer loading, annotated-statement plugin registration, advanced broker recovery and full shared trace remain open.
